population: healthy hospital-staff women 21–45 (mean 31.45±6.33), regular periods
phases_compared: early follicular (day 3±2) vs late follicular (day 12±2) vs mid-luteal (day 20±3), 2 cycles
main_result: Medians early/late follicular/mid-luteal: cycle 1 197/176/194, p=0.755; cycle 2 182/206/208, p=0.394 (Friedman)
risk_of_bias: some concerns – no hormone confirmation; 2 OC users (3.9%) included
notes: Moderately sized within-subject study over two cycles; no phase differences.

population: healthy hospital-staff women 21–45 (mean 31.45±6.33), regular periods
phases_compared: early follicular (day 3±2) vs late follicular (day 12±2) vs mid-luteal (day 20±3), 2 cycles
risk_of_bias: some concerns – no hormone confirmation; 2 OC users (3.9%) included
notes: Cycle 1 near-significant trend not repeated in cycle 2.

population: healthy hospital-staff women 21–45 (mean 31.45±6.33), regular periods
phases_compared: early follicular (day 3±2) vs late follicular (day 12±2) vs mid-luteal (day 20±3), 2 cycles
measure: skin surface pH (MPA-5), mean of 5 facial points
risk_of_bias: some concerns – no hormone confirmation; 2 OC users (3.9%) included
notes: pH outcome.

population: women 18–50 with acne complaint in last 30 days, dermatology practice
phases_compared: week before menses vs during vs after vs throughout cycle
main_result: 65% worse with menses; of these 56% week before, 17% during, 3% after, 24% throughout; 18–29y 68% vs 30–50y 42% (no p-values reported)
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall; OC users included (31, reported as 37%)
notes: Sites: forehead 42%, cheeks 42%, perioral 31%, entire face 41%. Full text read from PMC web page.

population: healthy premenopausal women (plus postmenopausal comparison)
measure: forearm local tissue water (tissue dielectric constant)
main_result: no significant cycle-dependent variation in tissue water (numbers not reported in abstract)
risk_of_bias: high – n=10 cycling women; forearm only; HC not stated
notes: Saliva estradiol/progesterone showed expected cycle pattern. Measures deeper tissue water, not stratum corneum hydration. Blood flow outcome not extracted.

population: volunteers receiving fractional CO2 laser
main_result: 2 developed hypopigmentation, 5 hyperpigmentation; PIH most severe when laser done just before or after menstruation (no statistics reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n=7; no statistics; phase method not stated
notes: Indexed as editorial. 'worse_menstrual' here means perimenstrual (just before or after menses).

population: healthy women 20±4 y and 42±3 y, normal 4-week cycles
measure: skin extensibility and relaxation time (extensometer), volar forearm
main_result: Young: extensibility time 86.4±9.5 (day 10) vs 79.6±10 (day 25), relaxation 109.1±11 vs 102±13, p<0.01; middle-aged: 100.8±14 vs 104±14, 121±12 vs 121±13, not significant
risk_of_bias: high – forearm only; HC not stated; calendar days; small groups
notes: Premenstrual change in young women only; authors attribute it to higher skin water content.

population: young women 18–25, population-based multistage random sample
phases_compared: before vs during vs after menses (acne flare timing, past 6 months)
main_result: 44.8% had acne; of acne patients 56.7% reported perimenstrual flare: 58.5% before menses, 35% during, 6.5% after
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall over 6 months; HC not reported
notes: Acne also associated with premenstrual and menstrual symptoms (adjusted ORs 1.23–1.63).

population: women 15–23 with mild acne, regular periods
phases_compared: seven 4-day periods of a standardised 28-day cycle (8 weekly measurements)
main_result: % of subject mean: 108.6±SE 5.2% (days 1–4) fell to 89.9±4.1% (days 13–16), P<0.02; rose to 111.8±5.1% (days 17–20), P<0.01; fell to 92.0±3.3% premenstrually (days 25–28), P<0.01
risk_of_bias: high – n=10; ovulation assumed by back-counting; variation small vs method error
notes: Nadir just after ovulation, peak early luteal, premenstrual fall. Only 2 measurements when acne worse; SER unchanged.

population: female acne patients 27–42
measure: reported premenstrual or menstrual exacerbation of acne
main_result: 71% with normal androgen levels and 72% with elevated androgens had premenstrual or menstrual exacerbation
risk_of_bias: high – n=26 clinic patients; self-report; no phase comparison design
notes: Elevated-androgen patients had premenstrual therapy-resistant nodules on chin. Premenstrual and menstrual flare not separated.

population: women with hidradenitis suppurativa
measure: self-reported premenstrual exacerbation of hidradenitis suppurativa
main_result: 22 of 36 experienced premenstrual exacerbation
risk_of_bias: high – HS patients; self-report; not a skincare outcome
notes: PMC copy is scanned images only; text not extractable. 19 had or had had acne.

population: patients with hidradenitis suppurativa (female preponderance 13:5)
measure: clinical history of premenstrual flare of hidradenitis suppurativa
main_result: premenstrual flare in 57 per cent of women
risk_of_bias: high – HS patients; self-report; not a skincare outcome
notes: No flare associated with irregular or anovulatory cycles; hormone profiles in 36 women.

population: women with seborrhoea and women with low sebum production
measure: Sebutape sebum excretion and number of active sebaceous glands
main_result: seborrhoeic women: cyclic changes with maximum sebum excretion in week before menstruation; low-sebum women: no changes (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n and statistics not reported in abstract; phase method not stated
notes: Premenstrual rise only in seborrhoeic subgroup.

population: healthy women with regular cycles
measure: sodium lauryl sulfate irritant patch test: visual score, TEWL, oedema, blood flow
main_result: response significantly stronger on day 1 than days 9–11: visual score p<0.05, TEWL p<0.05, oedema p<0.005
risk_of_bias: some concerns – no hormone confirmation; HC not stated in abstract
notes: Irritant susceptibility higher at menstruation. Test site not stated in abstract.

population: private-practice patients with acne and subclinical dermographism, mostly women 20–40
main_result: 'vast majority of women had premenstrual flares' (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – selected clinic series; self-report; no numbers
notes: Special subgroup (acne with dermographism); limited generalisability.

population: normal women
phases_compared: day of maximal oestrogen vs maximal progesterone vs minimal oestrogen/progesterone (just before menses)
main_result: TEWL higher on day of minimal oestrogen/progesterone vs maximal oestrogen: back p=0.037, forearm p=0.021
risk_of_bias: high – n not reported; 'putative' hormone days; non-facial sites
notes: Barrier less complete just before menses than just before ovulation.

population: normal women
phases_compared: day of maximal oestrogen vs maximal progesterone vs minimal oestrogen/progesterone (just before menses)
measure: methyl nicotinate vasodilation dose-response (IR, PR, AUC)
main_result: no significant differences in IR, PR or AUC across the 3 test days
risk_of_bias: high – n not reported; 'putative' hormone days; non-facial sites
notes: Baseline blood flow higher on maximal-progesterone day (back p=0.021, forearm p=0.009); thermoregulation, not extracted as outcome.

population: women with and without acne (methods paper)
phases_compared: premenstrual vs menstrual phase (women with acne)
measure: skin surface lipids by enzymatic assay (glycerol esters, FFAs, cholesterol/esters)
main_result: women with acne in premenstrual phase had increased glycerol esters, FFAs and cholesterol/esters vs menstrual phase (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – assay-validation paper; n and statistics not reported; likely between-person
notes: Cross-sectional comparison assumed; design not clear from abstract.

population: women with hidradenitis suppurativa (8 postmenopausal)
main_result: premenstrual flare reported by 32 women; not related to menstrual disturbances
risk_of_bias: high – HS patients; self-report; not a skincare outcome
notes: Denominator includes some postmenopausal women.

population: female participants 12–52 asked about their acne
phases_compared: before vs during vs after menses vs unrelated
main_result: 44% (177/400) reported premenstrual flares; OC use, severity, ethnicity did not affect rate; >33y higher than 20–33y (P=.03)
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall; OC users included
notes: Most-cited prevalence figure for premenstrual acne flare.

population: adult women 25–40, general population
main_result: premenstrual flare recorded as causing acne in 78% of acne subjects
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall; postal survey
notes: Total acne prevalence 41% (17% acne, 24% 'physiological acne').

population: nickel-sensitive women
measure: nickel patch test (Finn Chamber) reaction severity
main_result: reactions more severe on days 20–24 than days 7–10 in both groups, but not statistically significant
risk_of_bias: some concerns – no hormone confirmation; HC not stated
notes: Allergic (not irritant) reactivity; non-significant luteal trend.

n_total: 41 enrolled; 18 did not complete; 48 evaluation points (25 cycle 1, 23 cycle 2)
population: women 18–44 (mean 31±7.9) with ≥3 inflammatory lesions, untreated, regular menses
phases_compared: late follicular (day 7–12) vs late luteal (day 22–28), 2 cycles
main_result: inflammatory lesions 9.5 to 11.9 (+25.3%), P=.02; comedones 9.2 to 11.1 (+21.2%), P=.05; inflammatory increase in 63% (30) of evaluations
risk_of_bias: some concerns – 18/41 dropouts; no hormone confirmation; OC not mentioned
notes: Self-described case series; the main quantified premenstrual acne-flare study.

population: healthy Caucasian women 21–48 with 26–29 day cycles
phases_compared: weekly measurements over 2–3 months, by cycle day
main_result: barrier weakest between days 22 and 26 (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n and statistics not reported; industry (Estée Lauder); HC not stated
notes: Several small studies pooled in one report.

population: healthy Caucasian women 21–48 with 26–29 day cycles
phases_compared: weekly measurements over 2–3 months, by cycle day
main_result: skin driest between day 1 and day 6 (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n and statistics not reported; industry (Estée Lauder); HC not stated

population: healthy Caucasian women 21–48 with 26–29 day cycles
phases_compared: weekly measurements over 2–3 months, by cycle day
main_result: lipid secretion appeared highest on days 16–20 (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n and statistics not reported; industry (Estée Lauder); HC not stated
notes: Peak is early-to-mid luteal, not premenstrual.

population: healthy Caucasian women 21–48 with 26–29 day cycles
phases_compared: weekly measurements over 2–3 months, by cycle day
measure: lactic acid sting response; UVB minimal erythemal dose
main_result: sting response did not vary much with cycle; high UVB susceptibility days 20–28 (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n and statistics not reported; industry (Estée Lauder); HC not stated
notes: Sensory reactivity flat; UV sensitivity higher in luteal phase.

population: healthy Caucasian women 21–48 with 26–29 day cycles
phases_compared: weekly measurements over 2–3 months, by cycle day
main_result: highest microbial count around days 16–22 (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n and statistics not reported; industry (Estée Lauder); HC not stated
notes: Culture count; not sequencing.

population: middle-aged general population (SU.VI.MAX cohort)
measure: questionnaire pattern IV: 'breakout of spots' related to menstrual cycle
main_result: pattern IV reported by 49% of premenopausal women
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall; timing within cycle not specified
notes: Classed as acne-type breakouts; exact phase not specified. Premenopausal denominator not stated in abstract.

population: volunteers (30 men, 30 women)
main_result: pore size significantly increased during ovulation phase (P=0.008)
risk_of_bias: high – about 30 women, between-person; phase method not stated
notes: Described as 'prospective, randomized, controlled'. Sebum by phase not reported.

population: untreated acne patients 13–42 at dermatology clinics
measure: questionnaire: perceived effect of menstrual cycle on acne
main_result: menstrual cycle (females n=83): worse 97.6%, no effect 2.4%; 'premenstrual exacerbation of acne was experienced by 97.6%'
risk_of_bias: high – self-report belief; clinic sample
notes: Very high figure; question measured belief rather than observed flares.

population: women 19–40 (within wider age/sex sample)
measure: cerumen (ear wax) lipid composition by HPTLC
main_result: follicular samples had significantly lower free fatty acids and higher cholesterol and squalene vs luteal or menstrual (numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – ear canal not facial skin; n not reported; between-person
notes: Indirect (cerumen glands); low relevance to facial skin.

population: high-school pupils aged 16±0.9
measure: clinical acne grading plus questionnaire on menstruation
main_result: premenstrual phase identified as a risk factor for moderate-to-severe acne (effect size not reported in abstract)
risk_of_bias: high – self-report; abstract only
notes: Full text (JID) blocked (403).

population: hospital acne patients, mean age 19.78
main_result: 79 of 137 female patients (57.7%) gave a history of premenstrual flare
risk_of_bias: high – self-report history; clinic sample; OC not mentioned
notes: Face involved in all patients. No association testing.

population: acne outpatients 11–35
main_result: premenstrual flare seen in 70% of female patients
risk_of_bias: high – self-report history; clinic sample
notes: Described as prospective clinic series.

population: adolescents 13–19 at two schools
main_result: of 555 female respondents with acne, 39.1% reported flares in temporal proximity to menstruation
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall
notes: Timing described as 'proximity to menstruation', not split into before/during.

population: asthmatic women of fertile age
measure: symptom questionnaire during a single cycle (acne among 'edematous' symptoms)
main_result: practically all monitored symptoms increased premenstrually vs preovulatory; acne-specific result not reported in abstract
risk_of_bias: high – asthma population; acne not reported separately
notes: Indirect population; acne one of many symptoms.

population: adults >25 with acne, tertiary hospital
main_result: premenstrual flare seen in 27 (11.7%) of female patients
risk_of_bias: high – self-report history; clinic sample; OC not mentioned
notes: Much lower than other series; authors contrast with 84.8% elsewhere.

population: high-school students, Bangkok
main_result: more than half believed pre-menstrual period (among other factors) aggravated their acne; exact figure not reported
risk_of_bias: high – belief questionnaire; no specific number
notes: Denominator for the premenstrual item unclear (may include boys).

population: women mean 23.36 y (SD 4.94)
phases_compared: daily photographs across an adjusted 28-day cycle (LH surge = day 14)
measure: cheek redness (L:M cone ratio) and luminance from calibrated photographs
main_result: redness varied χ2(4)=18.02, p=0.0012: fell after menses onset, rose in week 2, stayed high through luteal phase; luminance not significant; all JNDs <1 (not visible)
risk_of_bias: low – urinary LH confirmed, HC excluded, calibrated objective measure; small n
notes: Changes too small for human eye to detect.

population: young adult women with declared premenstrual acne flares
main_result: premenstrual flare: papules 20.2 vs 13.7 (p=0.0008); closed comedones 25.6 vs 22.7 (p=0.04)
risk_of_bias: some concerns – selected flare-reporters; phase method and HC unclear in abstract
notes: Then RCT half-face: dermocosmetic vs placebo in luteal phase, inflammatory lesions 7.6 vs 9.4 (p=0.01). Not timed vs steady routine.

population: women with mild-to-moderate acne, regular cycles, no hormonal pathology
phases_compared: 50% glycolic peel in days 1–7 vs days 10–14 vs last 10 days of cycle (3 groups of 10)
measure: acne severity score after 3 months of peels
main_result: scores decreased in all groups; statistically significant only in the days 10–14 (ovulation) group
risk_of_bias: high – n=10 per group; randomisation not stated; no steady-routine control
notes: Only phase-timed skincare study; 'higher_at_ovulation' = greatest treatment benefit when peel given days 10–14.

population: women of reproductive age, including 250 healthy hospital workers
measure: standardised questionnaire: lesions increased during menstrual period
main_result: acneiform lesion was the most commonly reported menstrual-exacerbated symptom: Behçet's 51%, healthy controls 62%
risk_of_bias: high – self-report (authors' stated limitation)
notes: Healthy-control figure most relevant to the review.

population: women 16–50 in 4 age groups
main_result: luteal-phase moisture 93.5% (youngest) to 115.5% (oldest) of standard index; r2=0.45 E2–moisture on day 5 in 40–50y only; phase difference not reported
risk_of_bias: high – direct day-5 vs day-25 comparison not reported; small age subgroups; HC not stated
notes: Serum oestradiol measured but used for correlation, not phase confirmation.

population: women 16–50 in 4 age groups
risk_of_bias: high – direct day-5 vs day-25 comparison not reported; small age subgroups; HC not stated
notes: Age and oestradiol comparisons, not phase comparisons.

population: women 16–50 in 4 age groups
main_result: not reported
risk_of_bias: high – direct day-5 vs day-25 comparison not reported; small age subgroups; HC not stated
notes: Discoloration measured but no result given in abstract.

population: women 21–45 with recurrent vulval folliculitis ('vulval acne')
main_result: 9 patients reported a cyclical pattern, premenstrual exacerbation most common
risk_of_bias: high – retrospective; n=16; non-facial
notes: Non-facial acne-like condition.

population: adult acne patients >25 among 24,056 adult attendees
main_result: premenstrual flare in 61.9% of female patients
risk_of_bias: high – self-report history; clinic sample
notes: Labelled 'prospective, observational'; effectively cross-sectional history-taking.

population: adult female acne patients ≥25 (mean 31.8±7.1)
main_result: pre-menstruation reported as aggravating factor by 72.6%; premenstrual flare associated with PCOS (univariate and multivariate)
risk_of_bias: high – self-report; 48.1% had PCOS (not natural-cycle healthy)
notes: High PCOS share limits relevance to healthy cycles.

population: adult female acne patients 25–67 (mean 33.4)
main_result: not reported
risk_of_bias: high – self-report; result absent from abstract
notes: Premenstrual flare was a stated aim but no figure in abstract; full text not accessible.

population: women with hormonal acne-prone skin, Chinese and Caucasian
phases_compared: different menstrual cycle phases (not specified in abstract)
main_result: changes in TEWL between and within hormonal phases (direction and numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n, phases and statistics not reported in abstract; industry (Oriflame) pilot
notes: Pilot study; full text blocked.

population: women with hormonal acne-prone skin, Chinese and Caucasian
phases_compared: different menstrual cycle phases (not specified in abstract)
main_result: changes in sebum level (direction and numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n, phases and statistics not reported in abstract; industry (Oriflame) pilot

population: women with hormonal acne-prone skin, Chinese and Caucasian
phases_compared: different menstrual cycle phases (not specified in abstract)
main_result: changes in hydration (direction and numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n, phases and statistics not reported in abstract; industry (Oriflame) pilot

population: women with hormonal acne-prone skin, Chinese and Caucasian
phases_compared: different menstrual cycle phases (not specified in abstract)
main_result: Cutibacterium, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus most abundant, without significant abundance differences within the menstrual cycle
risk_of_bias: high – n, phases and statistics not reported in abstract; industry (Oriflame) pilot
notes: Ethnic differences in metabolic pathways in follicular phase.

population: women with hormonal acne-prone skin, Chinese and Caucasian
phases_compared: different menstrual cycle phases (not specified in abstract)
main_result: changes in pore volume (direction and numbers not reported)
risk_of_bias: high – n, phases and statistics not reported in abstract; industry (Oriflame) pilot

population: adult female acne patients 26–41
main_result: 50% had history of premenstrual flare-up
risk_of_bias: high – self-report history; clinic sample
notes: Listed as open access but publisher blocked (403).

population: healthy women 18–65; cycling group mean 27.06±5.60 y, regular 25–31 day cycles
phases_compared: ovulatory (within 24 h of urinary LH surge) vs mid-luteal (7 days after ovulation)
main_result: TEWL 8.87±1.59 ovulatory vs 9.92±1.37 mid-luteal, p<0.001
risk_of_bias: some concerns – urinary LH only; n=36; measurement site not stated; text/table mismatch
notes: No change over 7 days in postmenopausal group (p=0.338).

population: healthy women 18–65; cycling group mean 27.06±5.60 y, regular 25–31 day cycles
phases_compared: ovulatory (within 24 h of urinary LH surge) vs mid-luteal (7 days after ovulation)
main_result: SH 40.55±7.80 ovulatory vs 36.27±7.42 mid-luteal, p=0.005 (as in text; Table 2 lists 36.27/36.72)
risk_of_bias: some concerns – urinary LH only; n=36; measurement site not stated; text/table mismatch
notes: Text and Table 2 values disagree; direction per text and abstract.

population: healthy women 18–65; cycling group mean 27.06±5.60 y, regular 25–31 day cycles
phases_compared: ovulatory (within 24 h of urinary LH surge) vs mid-luteal (7 days after ovulation)
main_result: SS-10 10.75 ovulatory vs 10.00 mid-luteal, p=0.601
risk_of_bias: some concerns – urinary LH only; n=36; measurement site not stated; text/table mismatch
notes: Self-rated dryness (3.51 vs 3.52, p=0.962) and itch (1.62 vs 1.86, p=0.378) also unchanged.

population: female graduate students, mean 24.9 y, regular 21–35 day cycles
phases_compared: premenstrual symptoms (PSST) only; no comparison phase
main_result: acne flare-ups reported premenstrually by 40.4% (abstract: 40.35%) of 285
risk_of_bias: high – self-report recall; 4.6% contraceptive and 13% menstrual-delaying medicine users included
notes: PMS-focused study; acne a secondary item.

population: healthy Chinese women 24–29, no acne, self-declared 26–30 day cycles
phases_compared: ovulation vs early luteal (all); plus follicular and late luteal (high-sebum group)
measure: sebum lipid composition (Sebutape; GC-MS/LC-MS), forehead and cheeks
main_result: menstrual-phase effect significant in high-sebum forehead data (ASCA p=0.003); sebaceous lipids peaked at ovulation and declined in early luteal phase
risk_of_bias: some concerns – n=19 per group; industry funded (P&G); HC not explicit
notes: Composition, not total output. Urinary ovulation tests used. Epidermal lipids stayed high after ovulation.

population: female college students 17–29, all mild acne (grade I–II), regular and irregular cycles
main_result: no significant difference between regular-cycle menstrual and intermenstrual samples; only significant pair Irregular-Menstrual vs Regular-Menstrual (R2=0.0179, p<0.001)
risk_of_bias: high – no hormone measures; phase definition not stated; HC not stated; low-biomass sampling
notes: Differences driven by irregular-cycle group. Regular-cycle Procrustes M2=0.221, p=0.877.

population: female college students 17–29, all mild acne (grade I–II), regular and irregular cycles
main_result: menstrual phase 57 grade I, 38 grade II; intermenstrual 58 grade I, 37 grade II (no test reported)
risk_of_bias: high – no hormone measures; phase definition not stated; HC not stated; low-biomass sampling
notes: Descriptive counts only; excluded acne grade 3 or higher.
